horizon_risk.caveat: Block-bootstrap simulation of the real P2-governed 6-leg ladder (same compute_sizing() the live watchdogs call), NOT a live-account realized track record. mdd_*_pct_of_terminal_equity is MDD-dollars as a share of THIS HORIZON'S OWN median terminal equity, not peak-to-trough max-drawdown-% (the dollar MDD columns are the non-decreasing, true first-passage figures; verify against those if the pct columns ever look wrong) -- the key read is that the dollar MDD generally grows as the ladder scales up, but it shrinks as a SHARE of the (also-growing) account -- that's the 'getting safer as we scale' effect, and where it stops improving is worth watching, not assuming. The _k05 columns are the frozen surplus-aggression overlay candidate (P0=$50k, B=$20k, k=0.5 -- same policy scripts/compute_p2_sizing.py actually deploys live), run on the SAME sampled paths as the plain-P2 columns so they're directly comparable. The _6e columns are the 6E (Euro FX) PROMOTED RESEARCH CANDIDATE, NOT LIVE (see memory/6e_promoted_research_candidate_2026_10_17.md) -- frozen architecture: signal on 6E.v.0, size in full-size 6E-equivalent units (qty = the shared ladder level), ladder scaled to ladder_scale_6e (this sample's risk-matched answer, not a parameter to defend exactly) to hold total portfolio variance roughly constant while redirecting that risk into 6E. Still mid operational-parity checklist (margin confirmed; contract-resolution matcher wiring, shadow run, and staged rollout not done) -- this is a research projection of a candidate, not a claim about what's actually running. The real underlying data pool is ~3.25 years (818 trading days); horizons beyond that (48/60 months) are block-bootstrap resampling of that same pool, not additional real history -- treat them as a longer extrapolation under the same statistical assumptions, with correspondingly less confidence than the shorter horizons. Where level_capped is true, the median path's ladder qty has hit MAX_LEVEL (a sanity ceiling against a misparsed equity read, not a real policy cap) -- that row understates the formula's own growth AND implies a contract count far past any real broker/market capacity question, so treat it as 'the model ran out of room,' not a real projection. The _staged columns are the LEADING combined-policy candidate: k=0.5 overlay runs unscaled from the start (ladder never shrunk), 6E stays OFF until equity first reaches e6_activation_threshold ($100k = 2x the original $50k protected principal -- an economically pre-defensible milestone, not a fitted parameter), then switches on PERMANENTLY (sticky -- does not deactivate if equity later dips back below), sized from REAL equity, never the overlay's inflated E_eff. A paired comparison (same bootstrap draws) found this captures ~84% of always-on 6E's incremental median terminal wealth while cutting the rate of a NEW sub-$50k breach that Wheel+k=0.5 alone wouldn't have hit from 5.3% to 0.1% -- an always-on combination of 6E+k=0.5 (tested, not shown here) is actively WORSE than 6E alone on both terminal wealth and MDD once properly risk-matched, so this staged gate -- not a shared risk budget -- is the mechanism that makes the combination work.
